column4: The section names duha as the forenoon time; at the contest with Pharaoh, the people are gathered «ضُحًى», making that named daylight hour a public scene.
The section says duha is sunlight as well as heat; the oath «وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا» directly joins the sun to its forenoon brightness.
The section's meal stands against undernourishment; this verse says the Lord of the House fed Quraysh «مِّن جُوعٍ» and secured them from fear, a concrete provision parallel.
The section joins forenoon sunlight to heat; this passage describes the sun as the guide to an extended shadow, adding the sun's changing shade as a specific counterpoint to exposure.
The section brings together forenoon warmth and food; here God shades Israel with clouds and provides manna and quail to eat, joining bodily cover and a meal in one provision scene.
This repeated wilderness scene pairs cloud shade with manna and quail and the command to eat from God's provision; it gives another specific meeting of protection and food.
The section's B003 meal sense evokes a table; the disciples ask Jesus for «مَائِدَةً مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ», a concrete table scene of requested provision.
The next ayah says the disciples want to eat from the table and have their hearts reassured; it specifies the table's food and purpose.
Jesus prays that the table be a feast for the first and last of them and a sign; this ayah makes the requested table a shared meal and gift.
God answers that He will send the table down, then warns of punishment for disbelief; this completes the provision scene with its stated boundary.
The section pairs sun-light with cooking fire; this lamp image says its oil nearly shines «وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ», sharply separating illumination from flame.
The section's dictionary branches name a camel-meat dish and a heated-milk dish; this verse puts drink from livestock beside eating from them, linking both ingredients to provided nourishment.
The section forbids overpowering the orphan; this command identifies consuming or exchanging an orphan's property as a concrete form of the prohibited harm.
The section's qahr line sets a boundary on harm to the orphan; this ayah specifies that boundary for the orphan's property, which must not be approached except in the best way until maturity.
This repeated property command makes the orphan-protection in the section concrete: do not approach the orphan's wealth except in the best manner until maturity.
After 22:36's camel meat is eaten and shared, this ayah says its meat and blood do not reach God, but piety does; it marks the limit of the section's physical cooking image.
The section's noon sun and cooking fire carry warmth; this passage begins with faces in «نَارًا حَامِيَةً», turning heat into punishment.
The next ayah gives them drink from «عَيْنٍ آنِيَةٍ», a boiling spring; it continues the burning scene with scalding liquid.
After the boiling spring, this ayah says there is no food except a thorny plant; it reverses the section's nourishing meal.
The next ayah specifies that the thorny food neither nourishes nor relieves hunger, an exact counterpart to the section's meal against poor nutrition.
The section's duha heat and cooking-fire images have a punitive counterpart in «سَمُومٍ وَحَمِيمٍ», scorching wind and boiling water.
The next ayah gives the punished a shade of black smoke, extending the hot scene into a shade that offers no relief.
This continuation says that shade is «لَا بَارِدٍ وَلَا كَرِيمٍ», explicitly withholding cooling or comfort against the section's bodily warmth and food.
After the Zaqqum and hot drink in 37:66–67, this ayah says their return is to the blazing fire; it completes the harmful-meal scene.
After the Zaqqum and boiling drink in 56:52–55, «هَٰذَا نُزُلُهُمْ» calls this their reception on Judgment Day, a pointed reversal of a welcoming meal.
